sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato droṇe hate rājan duryodhanamukhā nṛpāḥ bhṛśam udvignamanaso droṇaputram upāgaman
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, when Droṇa had been slain, the kings led by Duryodhana, their minds sorely troubled, came to Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: te droṇam upaśocantaḥ kaśmalābhihataujasaḥ paryupāsanta śokārtās tataḥ śāradvatīsutam
english: Grieving for Droṇa, their vigour struck down by despair, stricken with sorrow they gathered round the son of Śāradvatī's daughter.

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ te samāśvāsya hetubhiḥ śāstrasaṃmitaiḥ rātryāgame mahīpālāḥ svāni veśmāni bhejire
english: Having for a while consoled one another with reasons drawn from the scriptures, when night came on those guardians of the earth withdrew to their own quarters.

sanskrit: viśeṣataḥ sūtaputro rājā caiva suyodhanaḥ duḥśāsano 'tha śakunir na nidrām upalebhire
english: Above all the son of the charioteer, and King Suyodhana, and Duḥśāsana, and Śakuni could find no sleep.

sanskrit: te veśmasv api kauravya pṛthvīśā nāpnuvan sukham cintayantaḥ kṣayaṃ tīvraṃ nidrāṃ naivopalebhire
english: Even within their dwellings, O Kaurava, those lords of the earth found no ease; brooding on the dire ruin, they could not sleep at all.

sanskrit: sahitās te niśāyāṃ tu duryodhananiveśane atipracaṇḍād vidveṣāt pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Gathered together that night in Duryodhana's abode, out of their fierce and burning hatred for the high-souled Pāṇḍavas,

sanskrit: yat tad dyūtaparikliṣṭāṃ kṛṣṇām āninyire sabhām tat smaranto 'nvatapyanta bhṛśam udvignacetasaḥ
english: recalling how they had dragged Kṛṣṇā, tormented by the dice-game, into the assembly hall, they were filled with remorse, their minds sorely distressed.

sanskrit: cintayantaś ca pārthānāṃ tān kleśān dyūtakāritān kṛcchreṇa kṣaṇadāṃ rājan ninyur abdaśatopamām
english: And brooding on those afflictions of the sons of Pṛthā that the dice-game had wrought, O king, they passed the night in misery, and it seemed to them as long as a hundred years.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāte vimale sthitā diṣṭasya śāsane cakrur āvaśyakaṃ sarve vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then in the clear dawn, abiding under the rule of fate, they all performed their necessary rites with the observances ordained by scripture.

sanskrit: te kṛtvāvaśyakāryāṇi samāśvasya ca bhārata yogam ājñāpayām āsur yuddhāya ca viniryayuḥ
english: Having done their needful tasks and taken heart again, O Bhārata, they gave the order to array the troops and marched out for battle.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ senāpatiṃ kṛtvā kṛtakautukamaṅgalāḥ vācayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān dadhipātraghṛtākṣataiḥ
english: Having made Karṇa their commander, performing the auspicious rites of consecration, having the foremost of the twice-born pronounce blessings over them with bowls of curds, clarified butter, and unbroken grains,

sanskrit: niṣkair gobhir hiraṇyena vāsobhiś ca mahādhanaiḥ vardhyamānā jayāśīrbhiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ
english: honoured with gold coins, with cattle, with gold, and with garments of great worth, and exalted with benedictions of victory by bards, minstrels, and panegyrists,

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan kṛtasarvāhṇikakriyāḥ śibirān niryayū rājan yuddhāya kṛtaniścayāḥ
english: likewise the Pāṇḍavas, O king, having completed all their daily observances, marched out from their camp, O king, resolved upon battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca parasparavadhaiṣiṇām
english: Then there broke out a tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, each side seeking the slaughter of the other.

sanskrit: tayor dve divase yuddhaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ karṇe senāpatau rājann abhūd adbhutadarśanam
english: For two days the battle of those two armies, the Kuru and the Pāṇḍava hosts, raged on while Karṇa was commander, O king, a wondrous sight to behold.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrukṣayaṃ kṛtvā sumahāntaṃ raṇe vṛṣaḥ paśyatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ phalgunena nipātitaḥ
english: Then, when the Bull among men had wrought a very great destruction of the foe in battle, he was struck down by Phalguna before the very eyes of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons.

sanskrit: tatas tat saṃjayaḥ sarvaṃ gatvā nāgāhvayaṃ puram ācakhyau dhṛtarāṣṭrāya yad vṛttaṃ kurujāṅgale
english: Then Saṃjaya, going to the city named after the elephant, related the whole of it to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all that had come to pass in the land of the Kurus.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca āpageyaṃ hataṃ śrutvā droṇaṃ ca samare paraiḥ yo jagāma parām ārtiṃ vṛddho rājāmbikāsutaḥ
english: Janamejaya said: When the aged king, the son of Ambikā, heard that the son of the river-goddess and Droṇa had been slain in battle by their foes, and was plunged into the deepest anguish—

sanskrit: sa śrutvā nihataṃ karṇaṃ duryodhanahitaiṣiṇam kathaṃ dvijavara prāṇān adhārayata duḥkhitaḥ
english: when he heard that Karṇa too, who sought Duryodhana's welfare, was slain, how, O best of the twice-born, did he in his grief sustain his life?

sanskrit: yasmiñ jayāśāṃ putrāṇām amanyata sa pārthivaḥ tasmin hate sa kauravyaḥ kathaṃ prāṇān adhārayat
english: That king reposed his sons' hope of victory in Karṇa; when he was slain, how did the Kaurava keep his life within him?

sanskrit: durmaraṃ bata manye 'haṃ nṛṇāṃ kṛcchre 'pi vartatām yatra karṇaṃ hataṃ śrutvā nātyajaj jīvitaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Hard to die indeed, I think, is it for men, even those who dwell in misery, since on hearing that Karṇa was slain the king did not yet give up his life.

sanskrit: tathā śāṃtanavaṃ vṛddhaṃ brahman bāhlikam eva ca droṇaṃ ca somadattaṃ ca bhūriśravasam eva ca
english: So too the aged son of Śaṃtanu, O brahmin, and Bāhlika as well, and Droṇa, and Somadatta, and Bhūriśravas—

sanskrit: tathaiva cānyān suhṛdaḥ putrapautrāṃś ca pātitān śrutvā yan nājahāt prāṇāṃs tan manye duṣkaraṃ dvija
english: and likewise his other friends, and his sons and grandsons struck down—that on hearing of these he did not let his life go, that, O twice-born one, I deem a thing hard to do.

sanskrit: etan me sarvam ācakṣva vistareṇa tapodhana na hi tṛpyāmi pūrveṣāṃ śṛṇvānaś caritaṃ mahat
english: Tell me all this in full, O you whose wealth is austerity; for I am not sated, hearing the great deeds of the men of old.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hate karṇe mahārāja niśi gāvalgaṇis tadā dīno yayau nāgapuram aśvair vātasamair jave
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Karṇa was slain, O great king, the son of Gavalgaṇa, downcast, set out that night for the city of the elephant with horses swift as the wind.

sanskrit: sa hāstinapuraṃ gatvā bhṛśam udvignamānasaḥ jagāma dhṛtarāṣṭrasya kṣayaṃ prakṣīṇabāndhavam
english: Reaching Hāstinapura, his mind sorely troubled, he went to the dwelling of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, now bereft of its kinsmen.

sanskrit: sa samudvīkṣya rājānaṃ kaśmalābhihataujasam vavande prāñjalir bhūtvā mūrdhnā pādau nṛpasya ha
english: Beholding the king, his vigour struck down by despair, with joined palms he made his obeisance, and touched the king's feet with his head.

sanskrit: saṃpūjya ca yathānyāyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpatim hā kaṣṭam iti coktvā sa tato vacanam ādade
english: And having honoured Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, as was due, and crying, "Alas, what calamity!", he then took up his speech.

sanskrit: saṃjayo 'haṃ kṣitipate kaccid āste sukhaṃ bhavān svadoṣeṇāpadaṃ prāpya kaccin nādya vimuhyasi
english: "I am Saṃjaya, O lord of the earth. I trust your Majesty fares well. Having come to this disaster through your own fault, are you not today utterly bewildered?

sanskrit: hitāny uktāni viduradroṇagāṅgeyakeśavaiḥ agṛhītāny anusmṛtya kaccin na kuruṣe vyathām
english: Recalling the wholesome counsels spoken by Vidura, Droṇa, the son of Gaṅgā, and Keśava, counsels you did not heed—do you not now feel anguish?

sanskrit: rāmanāradakaṇvaiś ca hitam uktaṃ sabhātale nagṛhītam anusmṛtya kaccin na kuruṣe vyathām
english: Recalling the wholesome words spoken by Rāma, Nārada, and Kaṇva in the assembly hall, words you did not heed—do you not now feel anguish?

sanskrit: suhṛdas tvaddhite yuktān bhīṣmadroṇamukhān paraiḥ nihatān yudhi saṃsmṛtya kaccin na kuruṣe vyathām
english: Recalling your friends, devoted to your good and led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, slain in battle by the foe—do you not now feel anguish?"

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ rājā sūtaputraṃ kṛtāñjalim sudīrgham abhiniḥśvasya duḥkhārta idam abravīt
english: To the charioteer's son who spoke thus with joined palms, the king, drawing a long, deep sigh, stricken with grief, said this:

sanskrit: gāṅgeye nihate śūre divyāstravati saṃjaya droṇe ca parameṣvāse bhṛśaṃ me vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: "Now that the heroic son of Gaṅgā, who wielded divine weapons, has been slain, O Saṃjaya, and Droṇa too, that supreme bowman, my mind is sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: yo rathānāṃ sahasrāṇi daṃśitānāṃ daśaiva hi ahany ahani tejasvī nijaghne vasusaṃbhavaḥ
english: He who, born of the Vasus and full of splendour, day after day slew ten thousand mailed warriors on their chariots—

sanskrit: sa hato yajñasenasya putreṇeha śikhaṇḍinā pāṇḍaveyābhiguptena bhṛśaṃ me vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: that he was slain by Yajñasena's son Śikhaṇḍin, shielded by the Pāṇḍavas—at this my mind is sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: bhārgavaḥ pradadau yasmai paramāstraṃ mahātmane sākṣād rāmeṇa yo bālye dhanurveda upākṛtaḥ
english: He to whom, the high-souled one, the descendant of Bhṛgu gave the supreme weapon, he who in boyhood was instructed in the science of the bow by Rāma himself—

sanskrit: yasya prasādāt kaunteyā rājaputrā mahābalāḥ mahārathatvaṃ saṃprāptās tathānye vasudhādhipāḥ
english: by whose grace the sons of Kuntī, those mighty princes, and other lords of the earth as well, attained the rank of great chariot-warriors—

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃyuge satyasaṃdhaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ bhṛśaṃ me vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: hearing that this Droṇa, true to his word, that great bowman, was slain in battle by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, my mind is sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: trailokye yasya śāstreṣu na pumān vidyate samaḥ taṃ droṇaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā kim akurvata māmakāḥ
english: He whose equal in the science of arms was not to be found among men in all the three worlds—when they heard that this Droṇa was slain, what did my men do?

sanskrit: saṃśaptakānāṃ ca bale pāṇḍavena mahātmanā dhanaṃjayena vikramya gamite yamasādanam
english: When the host of the saṃśaptakas was sent, by the valour of the high-souled Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, to the abode of Yama,

sanskrit: nārāyaṇāstre nihate droṇaputrasya dhīmataḥ hataśeṣeṣv anīkeṣu kim akurvata māmakāḥ
english: and when the Nārāyaṇa weapon of the wise son of Droṇa had been undone, and the surviving ranks of the army stood, what did my men do?

sanskrit: vipradrutān ahaṃ manye nimagnaḥ śokasāgare plavamānān hate droṇe sannanaukān ivārṇave
english: I think them put to flight, sunk in an ocean of grief when Droṇa was slain, drifting like men whose ship has foundered upon the sea.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya bhojasya kṛtavarmaṇaḥ madrarājasya śalyasya drauṇeś caiva kṛpasya ca
english: Of Duryodhana, of Karṇa, of the Bhoja Kṛtavarman, of Śalya the king of the Madras, and of Droṇa's son, and of Kṛpa—

sanskrit: matputraśeṣasya tathā tathānyeṣāṃ ca saṃjaya viprakīrṇeṣv anīkeṣu mukhavarṇo 'bhavat katham
english: and of my surviving sons, and likewise of the others, O Saṃjaya—when their ranks were scattered, what hue was upon their faces?

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ yathā vṛttaṃ tattvaṃ gāvalgaṇe raṇe ācakṣva pāṇḍaveyānāṃ māmakānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Tell me, O son of Gavalgaṇa, all this just as it came to pass in battle, truly and in full, of both the Pāṇḍavas and my own men."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pāṇḍaveyair hi yad vṛttaṃ kauraveyeṣu māriṣa tac chrutvā mā vyathāṃ kārṣīd iṣṭe na vyathate manaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: What the Pāṇḍavas did to the Kauravas, O honoured one—hearing it, do not give way to anguish; over what is destined the mind is not afflicted.

sanskrit: yasmād abhāvī bhāvī vā bhaved artho naraṃ prati aprāptau tasya vā prāptau na kaś cid vyathate budhaḥ
english: Since whatever outcome is to befall a man, whether it shall come to pass or not, no wise man is troubled by its coming or its failing to come.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca na vyathā śṛṇvataḥ kā cid vidyate mama saṃjaya diṣṭam etat purā manye kathayasva yathecchakam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: No anguish whatever is in me as I listen, Saṃjaya; this, I think, was ordained long ago. Tell it as you will.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hate droṇe maheṣvāse tava putrā mahārathāḥ babhūvur āśvastamukhā viṣaṇṇā gatacetasaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When Droṇa the great bowman was slain, your sons, those mighty chariot-warriors, grew downcast of face, dejected, and bereft of spirit.

sanskrit: avāṅmukhāḥ śastrabhṛtaḥ sarva eva viśāṃ pate aprekṣamāṇāḥ śokārtā nābhyabhāṣan parasparam
english: With faces bowed down, those bearers of weapons, every one of them, O lord of peoples, not even looking at one another, stricken with grief, spoke not among themselves.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā vyathitākārān sainyāni tava bhārata ūrdhvam evābhyavekṣanta duḥkhatrastāny anekaśaḥ
english: Seeing them in their stricken aspect, your troops, O Bhārata, gazed only upward, oftentimes panicked with grief.

sanskrit: śastrāṇy eṣāṃ ca rājendra śoṇitāktāny aśeṣataḥ prābhraśyanta karāgrebhyo dṛṣṭvā droṇaṃ nipātitam
english: And their weapons, O lord of kings, all of them stained with blood, slipped from their fingertips at the sight of Droṇa struck down.

sanskrit: tāni baddhāny aniṣṭāni lambamānāni bhārata adṛśyanta mahārāja nakṣatrāṇi yathā divi
english: Those weapons, still bound to them yet unwelcome, hanging loose, O Bhārata, appeared, O great king, like the stars in the sky.

sanskrit: tathārtaṃ stimitaṃ dṛṣṭvā gatasattvam iva sthitam svaṃ balaṃ tan mahārāja rājā duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Seeing his own army thus stricken and motionless, standing as though its very life had gone out of it, O great king, King Duryodhana spoke:

sanskrit: bhavatāṃ bāhuvīryaṃ hi samāśritya mayā yudhi pāṇḍaveyāḥ samāhūtā yuddhaṃ cedaṃ pravartitam
english: "Relying upon the strength of your arms, I challenged the Pāṇḍavas to battle, and this war was set in motion.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ nihate droṇe viṣaṇṇam iva lakṣyate yudhyamānāś ca samare yodhā vadhyanti sarvataḥ
english: Now that Droṇa is slain, this host seems sunk in dejection; yet warriors who fight in battle are struck down on every side.

sanskrit: jayo vāpi vadho vāpi yudhyamānasya saṃyuge bhavet kim atra citraṃ vai yudhyadhvaṃ sarvatomukhāḥ
english: Whether victory or death befall the man who fights in battle—what marvel is there in that? Fight on, then, facing every quarter!

sanskrit: paśyadhvaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ yudhi pracarantaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ divyair astrair mahābalam
english: And behold the high-souled Karṇa, son of the Sun, that great bowman of mighty strength, ranging through the battle with his divine weapons!

sanskrit: yasya vai yudhi saṃtrāsāt kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ nivartate sadāmarṣāt siṃhāt kṣudramṛgo yathā
english: He, from dread of whom in battle Kuntī's son Dhanaṃjaya ever turns back in vexation, as a small beast from a lion—

sanskrit: yena nāgāyutaprāṇo bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ mānuṣeṇaiva yuddhena tām avasthāṃ praveśitaḥ
english: he by whom Bhīmasena, mighty in strength, with the vigour of ten thousand elephants, was brought to such a plight by mere human combat—

sanskrit: yena divyāstravic chūro māyāvī sa ghaṭotkacaḥ amoghayā raṇe śaktyā nihato bhairavaṃ nadan
english: he by whom that hero Ghaṭotkaca, knower of divine weapons and master of illusions, was slain in battle with the unfailing spear, even as he roared a fearsome roar—

sanskrit: tasya duṣpāravīryasya satyasaṃdhasya dhīmataḥ bāhvor draviṇam akṣayyam adya drakṣyatha saṃyuge
english: the inexhaustible might of the arms of that wise hero, true to his word and unconquerable in valour, you shall behold this day in battle.

sanskrit: droṇaputrasya vikrāntaṃ rādheyasyaiva cobhayoḥ pāṇḍupāñcālasainyeṣu drakṣyathāpi mahātmanoḥ
english: The prowess of both these high-souled ones, of Droṇa's son and of the son of Rādhā, you shall also behold amid the hosts of the Pāṇḍavas and the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: sarva eva bhavantaś ca śūrāḥ prājñāḥ kulodgatāḥ śīlavantaḥ kṛtāstrāś ca drakṣyathādya parasparam
english: And you yourselves, all of you—heroes, wise, nobly born, of good conduct, and skilled in arms—shall this day behold one another's deeds."

sanskrit: evam ukte mahārāja karṇo vaikartano nṛpaḥ siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ prāyudhyata mahābalaḥ
english: When this had been said, O great king, Karṇa, son of the Sun, the mighty prince, raising aloud a lion's roar, gave battle with all his great strength.

sanskrit: sa sṛñjayānāṃ sarveṣāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca paśyatām kekayānāṃ videhānām akarot kadanaṃ mahat
english: Before the eyes of all the Sṛñjayas, the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, and the Videhas, he wrought a great slaughter.

sanskrit: tasyeṣudhārāḥ śataśaḥ prādurāsañ śarāsanāt agre puṅkhe ca saṃsaktā yathā bhramarapaṅktayaḥ
english: From his bow there poured forth showers of arrows by the hundred, joined point to feathered shaft like ranks of bees.

sanskrit: sa pīḍayitvā pāñcālān pāṇḍavāṃś ca tarasvinaḥ hatvā sahasraśo yodhān arjunena nipātitaḥ
english: Having harried the Pāñcālas and the swift Pāṇḍavas, and having slain warriors by the thousand, he was at last struck down by Arjuna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ śokasyāntam apaśyan vai hataṃ matvā suyodhanam vihvalaḥ patito bhūmau naṣṭacetā iva dvipaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When he had heard this, O great king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra the son of Ambikā, seeing no end to his grief and believing Suyodhana slain, fell distraught upon the ground like an elephant bereft of consciousness.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmau vihvale rājasattame ārtanādo mahān āsīt strīṇāṃ bharatasattama
english: When that best of kings, distraught, had fallen upon the ground, there arose a great cry of anguish from the women, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa śabdaḥ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ pūrayām āsa sarvaśaḥ śokārṇave mahāghore nimagnā bharatastriyaḥ
english: That sound filled the whole earth on every side; the women of the Bharatas were plunged in a vast and terrible ocean of sorrow.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ ca samāsādya gāndhārī bharatarṣabha niḥsaṃjñā patitā bhūmau sarvāṇy antaḥpurāṇi ca
english: And drawing near to the king, O bull of the Bhāratas, Gāndhārī fell senseless to the ground, and so did all the women of the inner apartments.

sanskrit: tatas tāḥ saṃjayo rājan samāśvāsayad āturāḥ muhyamānāḥ subahuśo muñcantyo vāri netrajam
english: Then Saṃjaya, O king, comforted those stricken women, who were swooning again and again and shedding the water born of their eyes.

sanskrit: samāśvastāḥ striyas tās tu vepamānā muhur muhuḥ kadalya iva vātena dhūyamānāḥ samantataḥ
english: Though comforted, those women trembled again and again, shaken on every side like plantain trees buffeted by the wind.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ viduraś cāpi prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram āśvāsayām āsa tadā siñcaṃs toyena kauravam
english: And Vidura too then comforted the king, that lord whose only sight was wisdom, sprinkling the Kaurava with water.

sanskrit: sa labdhvā śanakaiḥ saṃjñāṃ tāś ca dṛṣṭvā striyo nṛpa unmatta iva rājā sa sthitas tūṣṇīṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Slowly regaining his senses, and beholding those women, O king, the king stood silent like one out of his mind, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tato dhyātvā ciraṃ kālaṃ niḥśvasaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ svān putrān garhayām āsa bahu mene ca pāṇḍavān
english: Then, having brooded a long while and sighing again and again, he reproached his own sons and held the Pāṇḍavas in high regard.

sanskrit: garhayitvātmano buddhiṃ śakuneḥ saubalasya ca dhyātvā ca suciraṃ kālaṃ vepamāno muhur muhuḥ
english: Having condemned his own judgement and that of Śakuni the son of Subala, and having pondered for a very long while, trembling again and again,

sanskrit: saṃstabhya ca mano bhūyo rājā dhairyasamanvitaḥ punar gāvalgaṇiṃ sūtaṃ paryapṛcchata saṃjayam
english: and having steadied his mind once more, the king, now possessed of fortitude, questioned again the charioteer Saṃjaya, the son of Gavalgaṇa.
